claims.text: TC4 has poor friction and wear performance under extreme-service conditions.
A thin Inconel 718 layer can be laser-clad between TC4 and a WMoTaNb-based refractory HEA top layer.
The Inconel 718 transition layer will form a compositionally graded interfacial zone in the TC4/Inconel 718/WMoTaNb-based system.
An inert cladding atmosphere will limit oxidation.
Controlling laser power, scanning speed, and preheat temperature will manage interdiffusion between the coating layers.
The Inconel 718 transition layer will provide strong metallurgical bonding between TC4 and the refractory HEA coating.
The Inconel 718 transition layer will provide thermal-expansion compatibility between TC4 and the refractory HEA top layer.
The Inconel 718 layer will minimize thermal residual stresses.
The Inconel 718 layer will promote controlled elemental diffusion at the interface.
The WMoTaNb-based refractory HEA top layer will develop a network of hard BCC and/or Laves-type phases.
The proposed hard-phase network will increase surface hardness and wear resistance.
The coating can develop the proposed hard-phase network without generating brittle intermetallic compounds.
The coating will approximately double surface hardness relative to untreated TC4.
The coating will produce markedly lower wear rates than untreated TC4 under high-contact-stress sliding.
The coating process will preserve the intrinsic core mechanical properties of the TC4 substrate.
Excessive interdiffusion can lead to brittle intermetallic-phase formation.
Carefully optimized laser-cladding parameters can prevent excessive interdiffusion and deleterious intermetallic formation.

contradictions.description: The mechanism anticipates a network that may contain Laves-type phases while also claiming that brittle intermetallic compounds will not form and treating intermetallic formation as deleterious. Laves phases are intermetallic compounds and are often brittle, so the intended distinction between beneficial Laves phase and deleterious intermetallic formation is not defined.
